main_text.l: uro fancienda[?], modò sint poffibilia, jus-
ta & honesta, Quinto, si aliquod sta-
tutum post juramentum præstitum abrog-
atum fuerit, vel in desuetudinem abe-
at; obligatio Juramenti quoad illud statutum
cessat, ita ut non teneatur illud
ultrà observare: nisi juratum fuerit verb-
is specialibus in ipsam rem statuto de-
retam; in eo enim casu sublato statuto
manet tamen obligatio. Sexto, cum
statuta Communitatum fere plurima
sint, & multa multis ignota; & difficill-
imum fit, imò vix possibile omnia &
singula exacto & examussim observare:
ut bona fide ita se comparaverit, ut nih-
il quod est officii sui lubens præterea-
t, debitamque adhibuerit moralem
diligentiam, ut ea omnia sciret quæ ad
ipsius officium pertinent; statuerintque
statui, honori, paci suæ Communitatis,
quantum humana patitur infirmitas, fi-
deliter & sine scandalo infervire; hunc
ego non dubitarem fidem de statutis obs-
ervandis à se datam bona conscientia
actenus liberasse, & debitum ad quod
obligavit, æqui boni lege exsolvisse.
Quod item & de publicis Regni legibus
intelligendum est.

page.notes: The scan cuts off the left edge of the text block, so the first letters of several lines are missing; the words there were completed from the context and marked [?] only where still doubtful (first word "fancienda"). The page number is printed in old style and read as 91 with doubt. The line-end hyphens "jus-", "prætterie-" and "ni-" are printed. The first letters of "sta-tutum", "Sexto", and "Quinto" are underlined or italic in the print, shown here as italic. Several long s characters are plain s as required; "est" is written as printed.
